test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 17 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
A statement is given followed by two assumptions numbered I and II. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true and decide which of the given assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

**Statement:**

Please register for the event latest by 21 April to collect free passes. Passes will not be issued without valid address proof.

**Assumptions:**

I. Voter ID card is a valid address proof.

II. Passes can be purchased at the venue.

options.text: Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit

solution:
**Statement:**

Please register for the event latest by 21 April to collect free passes. Passes will not be issued without valid address proof.

**Assumptions:**

**I. Voter ID card is a valid address proof.**

 
• The statement requires "valid address proof" but does not specify what constitutes it.
 
• While a Voter ID card is a common form of address proof.
 
• This assumption is **Not Implicit**.

**II. Passes can be purchased at the venue.**

 
• The statement focuses solely on "free passes" that are collected upon registration by a certain date. It provides no information about the possibility of purchasing passes, whether at the venue or elsewhere.
 
• The statement is limited to the process of obtaining free passes.
 
• Therefore, this assumption is **Not Implicit**.

**Neither assumption I nor II is implicit in the statement.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
